authority: Superintendent of Police (SP) / District Police Office / Commissioner of Police (for metropolitan areas)

description.en: A Character Certificate (also called Police Verification Certificate or Police Clearance Certificate for domestic purposes) is issued by the district police authority to certify that the applicant has no criminal record or pending criminal cases. It is commonly required for government job applications, educational admissions, passport verification, visa applications, and various other purposes.

verifiedConditions.claim: The applicant must be a resident of the district/police jurisdiction from where the character certificate is being sought. The certificate is issued based on police records of the local police station area.

The applicant must state a valid purpose for requiring the character certificate, such as government employment, educational admission, passport application, arms license, or any other official purpose.

unverifiedEligibility: Some states issue character certificates only for specific purposes (employment, education, arms license).
Persons with pending criminal cases may receive adverse remarks on their character certificate.
The character certificate is different from a Police Clearance Certificate (PCC) issued by the Passport Office for emigration purposes.
Some employers and institutions accept self-declarations in lieu of police character certificates.

requirements.claim: Prescribed application form available at the district police office, local police station, or downloadable from the state police website. Some states accept applications through the state services portal.
Aadhaar card, voter ID, passport, PAN card, or other government-issued identity document with photograph.
Proof of current residence — ration card, voter ID, Aadhaar card, electricity bill, or rent agreement showing the address within the police jurisdiction.
Recent passport-size photographs of the applicant (typically 2-4 copies).

Declaration or letter stating the purpose for which the character certificate is required. For employment purposes, a copy of the job offer or advertisement may be needed. For educational purposes, a letter from the institution may be required.
Self-declaration affidavit on stamp paper stating that the applicant has no criminal record or pending criminal cases. Required in some states.

processInformation.claim: Submit the application form with documents at the local police station or district police office. In many states, applications can be submitted online through the state police website or state services portal.

The local police station conducts a verification check against their criminal records database. A field visit or physical verification may be conducted to confirm the applicant's identity and address. The Station House Officer (SHO) or designated officer prepares the verification report.
The police station submits the verification report to the SP/Commissioner's office. The report indicates whether the applicant has any criminal antecedents or adverse entries.

The character certificate is issued by the SP/Commissioner's office or the designated authority. The certificate states that the applicant has no criminal record as per police records. In some states, the certificate can be downloaded online.

output.claim: A Character Certificate is issued on the letterhead of the SP/Commissioner of Police containing the applicant's personal details, address, purpose, and a statement regarding the criminal record status. The certificate typically has a validity of 6 months to 1 year from the date of issue.

fees.claim: Application fee varies from Rs. 50 to Rs. 200 depending on the state. Some states charge additional fees for urgency or stamp paper. Online applications may have a nominal portal service charge.

processingTime.applicability: Character certificate from application to issuance
processingTime.claim: Character certificate processing typically takes 7-21 days depending on the state, police station workload, and whether physical verification is required. Some states offer expedited processing for urgent cases (e.g., government job joining). Online applications may be processed faster.

sources.title: Bureau of Police Research and Development / State Police Portals
sources.publisher: Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPR&D), Ministry of Home Affairs / State Police Departments
sources.evidenceExcerpt: State police portals provide information on character certificate (police verification) procedures, required documents, fee details, and online application facilities. The process and requirements are broadly similar across states but the exact procedure, forms, and fees vary.
claimsSupported: Character certificates are issued by the SP/Commissioner of Police.
Police verification against criminal records is conducted before issuance.
Required documents include identity proof, address proof, and purpose declaration.
Fees vary by state, typically Rs. 50-200.
sources.uncertainty: Each state has its own police portal and procedures. A single representative source cannot cover all state variations.

limitations: This record provides a general overview. The exact process, forms, fees, and timelines vary significantly by state and police jurisdiction.

The record does not distinguish between a character certificate (general purpose) and a Police Clearance Certificate (PCC) for emigration/passport purposes, which follows a separate process through the Passport Office.
The record does not cover the process for applicants with criminal records or pending cases.
Online application availability varies by state. Not all states offer online character certificate applications.
Validity period of the certificate varies by state and purpose.
The record does not cover character certificates issued by educational institutions or employers.

review.reviewReason: General process verified from multiple state police portals. State-specific forms, fees, and online application processes need individual verification.
nextReviewTrigger: Introduction of centralized online character certificate portal.
Changes to police verification procedures (CCTNS integration).
